# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 75 (Bu-Vb Pc75)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc75  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 75  
**Title (English, from literature):** Raising a hand in anger  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Talasattika-sikkhāpada* ("Training rule on raising a hand in anger"), designated as Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 75 in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka, prohibits a Buddhist monk from physically threatening or gesturing violently against another monk out of anger. According to the rule's summary definition, a bhikkhu who gives into anger and makes a threatening gesture with a raised hand or palm toward another monk incurs an offense requiring formal confession (*pācittiya*). Shayne Clarke notes the rule in passing in a comparative enumeration of Vinaya prātimokṣa rules alongside its corresponding bhikkhunī counterpart [Clarke, Pārājika]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Corresponding rules exist in the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Pc 75), *Bhikkhu Parivāra* (Pc 75), *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Pc 153), and *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pc 153). External parallels survive in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan Vinaya texts across multiple monastic lineages, including the Sarvāstivāda (Chinese Pc 49; Sanskrit Prātimokṣa Pc 49), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit Pc 49), Mahīśāsaka (Chinese Pc 72), Dharmaguptaka (Chinese Pc 79), and Mahāsāṅghika/Lokottaravāda (Chinese and Sanskrit Pc 59), alongside corresponding nuns' rules in these schools.
